inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 507.54m ordinary shares on issue (annual report, 10-Jun-2026) + 3.0m unvested performance rights (FY26 diluted-EPS note, p.101); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The Jun-2025 A$367.4m placement/SPP (22.7m shares) is already in the count; no further non-SBC issuance modelled (DRP is small and neutralised)
inputs.net_debt_composition: net borrowings 1,069.5 (loans & borrowings 1,219.2 ex leases less cash 149.7, FY26 note 3 / p.30) + non-controlling interests 5.2 (NCI charged once, in the bridge). Lease liabilities 352.7 EXCLUDED: lease cash is charged inside the flows (treatment B)
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: OCF 485.7 less payments for PP&E 263.0 (FY26 cash flow statement, p.66); levered, post-IFRS16 (lease principal 100.6 sits in financing)
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, equity reserve movement note 8a: equity-settled share-based payment transactions 9.6 (FY25 10.4). No net-share-settlement tax line disclosed; awards are settled with on-market treasury-share purchases (A$22.5m FY26) that already sit inside operating cash flow, so deducting the 9.6 expense on top is mildly conservative
inputs.interest_income_note: A$7.0m FY26 interest received is NOT stripped: ALS carries A$1.07bn net debt, so no cash pile is added to EV and there is nothing to double-count. The component build is unlevered (EBITDA-based) so neither interest received nor the A$78.2m interest paid enters the projected flows; financing cost is charged through WACC and the net-debt bridge
inputs.buyback_note: No capital-management buyback (financing activities: nil). A$22.5m of treasury shares were bought on-market in FY26 to settle employee awards and are classified inside operating cash flow. Flat count is therefore funded
inputs.lease_treatment: B: leases as operating cost. Lease cash A$115.7m FY26 (principal 100.6 in financing + interest ~15.2 in operating; company reports 'ROU payments 115.7') charged as lease_cost_pct 3.5% of revenue inside the flows; lease liabilities 352.7 excluded from net debt; D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use amortisation (4.2% of revenue). This matches ALS's own covenant definitions (pre-IFRS16 underlying EBITDA 715.7, net debt ex leases 1,069.5)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-21T06:10:32Z (ASX regular close, 16:10 AEST; Yahoo v8 chart)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in AUD, the currency of the flows: AU 10-yr government ~4.4% risk-free, 5.5% equity risk premium, beta ~1.0 gives ~9.9% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5% (USPP book 3.7% fixed, marginal higher) is ~3.6% after 28% tax; market-value weights ~91/9 equity/debt give ~9.3%, rounded to 9.0%. Cyclicality, the cyber incident and Americas execution risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in an ad-hoc WACC premium, and the same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once)
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + section 7). ALS is a fee-for-service testing lab operator with an ordinary cash-flow statement; not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco/distressed shell. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry).

MID-CYCLE: FY26 is a record year at the top of a mineral-exploration up-cycle (Commodities 39% of revenue, ~64% of segment EBIT, 35.5% segment margin). Base-case margins are faded to a mid-cycle level rather than extrapolating FY26/FY27 guidance; the bear case carries an explicit FY28-29 down-cycle. Revenue growth is anchored to FY27 guidance, not to the 13.5% 5-yr revenue CAGR which includes Nuvisan/York acquisitions and the up-cycle.

ONE-OFFS: ALS excluded A$70.6m (FY26) and A$70.9m (FY25) of 'one-off' restructuring/greenfield cash from underlying earnings two years running. Base case charges half of that through the margin (~0.8pp), bear charges all, bull none.

COMPONENT BUILD: EBITDA (post-IFRS16, pre-SBC) - lease cash 3.5% - SBC 0.3% - D&A ex-ROU 4.2% = EBIT; cash tax 28% on positive EBIT; + D&A - capex (per-year path, FY27 = guided ~A$240m) + WC capture -12% of revenue change. FY0 check: 842.6 - 115.7 - 9.6 - 139.4 = 577.9 EBIT vs underlying EBIT pre-IFRS16 583.8 (599.0 - 15.2 ROU interest); NOPAT 416 vs underlying NPAT 381.2 + after-tax net interest ~50 = 431 -- ties within noise.

TERMINAL: max(0, min(Gordon, 18x FCF_10)). 18x (not the 20x compounder default) reflects blended cyclicality; Gordon binds in base (17.2x) and bear (15.8x), the cap binds in bull. Today's EV/owner-FCF is ~40x, so every scenario assumes multiple COMPRESSION, not expansion.
SBC-LIGHT: SBC is 0.3% of revenue. House and street bases differ by ~A$0.4/share; band_position set to null because the band is too narrow for the price's position in it to mean anything.
ASSOCIATES: investments in associates (dividends received A$8.8m FY26) are neither in the flows nor in the bridge -- a small unmodelled asset, conservative.

DATA: the FY2019 extracted annual report is a byte-identical duplicate of FY2018 (same md5); FY2019 figures come from the FY2020 report comparatives. FY2018 SBC is not in the corpus (immaterial, <A$3m).
PRICE: regular ASX close; not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 guidance blend (Commodities +13-15% x 39% + Life Sciences mid-single-digit x 61%), decelerating to 3%; cross-checked against equity 3-yr CAGR 7.3%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR 7.3% is 46% below revenue 3-yr CAGR 13.4% (acquisitions + up-cycle in revenue; dividends ~57% payout and the FY24 Nuvisan impairment hold book value back) and the 5-yr equity CAGR 9.6% is inflated by the Jun-2025 A$367m raise. Neither is used directly; growth is guidance-anchored.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC) 3-yr CAGR is -9.3% vs reported -8.8%: the FY26 base is depressed by the A$263m capex peak (7.9% of revenue vs 5.5-6.4% in FY23-25) as the hub-lab program peaked, not by SBC. SBC grew 7.9 -> 9.6 over three years (0.35% -> 0.29% of revenue): SBC is not outgrowing cash flow. Interest income is not stripped (net-debt company). FY2018 SBC unavailable (FY2019 file is a duplicate of FY2018); FY2019-FY2023 SBC backfilled into the CSV from filings on 2026-09-21.

base.ebitda_margin_basis: underlying EBITDA, post-IFRS16 (before lease cash), before SBC; FY26 actual 25.4% (833.0 + 9.6 SBC) / 3,320.1
base.narrative: FY27 tracks guidance (Commodities +13-15%, Life Sciences mid-single-digit, blended ~8%), then growth fades to 3% nominal AUD as the exploration up-cycle matures. Margin: FY27 25.8% pre-SBC post-IFRS16 (guided +130-150bps is offset by a ~0.8pp haircut for half of the recurring ~A$70m 'one-off' restructuring cash and Middle East/cyber costs), then mid-cycled to 25.0% (pre-IFRS16 owner ~21.2%, between FY25 20.3% and FY26 21.6%; FY19-FY22 ran 20-21%). Capex steps down from FY26's 7.9% to FY27 guidance ~A$240m (6.7%) and 5.5% once the A$230m hub program is done; working capital consumes 12% of incremental revenue (FY26: 18%, FY25: 6%).

bull.ebitda_margin_basis: underlying EBITDA, post-IFRS16 (before lease cash), before SBC; FY26 actual 25.4% (833.0 + 9.6 SBC) / 3,320.1
bull.narrative: Critical-minerals exploration up-cycle runs multi-year (electrification, AI power demand), PFAS and emerging-contaminant testing compounds mid-teens, Nuvisan savings and automation/AI lab productivity deliver the guided margin expansion for four years to 28.0% (pre-IFRS16 ~24.2%, SGS/Bureau Veritas territory), Americas Environmental is fixed and bolt-on M&A funded from a 1.5x balance sheet keeps growth at high-single digits for five years. Terminal growth 3.5%; capex stays ~5.8% to fund it.

bear.ebitda_margin_basis: underlying EBITDA, post-IFRS16 (before lease cash), before SBC; FY26 actual 25.4% (833.0 + 9.6 SBC) / 3,320.1
bear.narrative: Commodities down-cycle FY28-FY29: exploration budgets and junior-miner raisings fall, Minerals volumes and pricing compress (Commodities is 39% of revenue but ~64% of segment EBIT), Group revenue falls 6% in FY29 and margins trough at 21.5% (pre-IFRS16 ~17.7%). The May-2026 cyber incident costs clients and remediation spend, Americas Environmental (York) is never fixed, and the ~A$70m/yr of 'one-off' restructuring cash keeps recurring in full. Recovery to a 23.5% margin by FY32 (pre-IFRS16 ~19.7%, below FY26) and 3% growth; capex is cut to 5.2% once the hub program completes.

entry_price.method: price at which the scenario's 10-yr owner FCF plus a terminal value BUILT AT THE 15% HURDLE (min(Gordon@15%, 18x FCF_10)), less net debt, returns 15% IRR; per scenario, then probability-weighted

required_return_table.note: each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate; the 9% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base

sensitivity.note: rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; terminal value re-capped at 18x in every cell

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25% because the FY26 base sits at a cyclical earnings peak (record NPAT, Minerals margin 35.5%), a live cyber incident is unresolved, and management itself flagged slower junior-miner conversion and a Middle East supply-chain risk. Bull down to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once: a multi-year exploration up-cycle, four more years of guided margin expansion, and a fixed Americas Environmental business. No going-concern or covenant risk (1.5x leverage, 13.5x cover) so bear is not pushed higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is ~A$0.4/share wide (SBC 0.3% of revenue); the price sits far above both, so band position is not meaningful and is set to null

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF DCF, SBC expensed, leases charged in the flows (treatment B), mid-cycled margins, 10-year horizon, terminal value capped at 18x, risk carried in scenario flows and weights rather than in a scenario-specific WACC.
valuation_philosophy.key_finding: At A$21.35 ALS trades at ~28x underlying EPS and ~16.7x EV/pre-IFRS16 EBITDA on peak-cycle earnings. The weighted owner-FCF value is A$11.33; even the bull case (A$15.95) sits below the price. The market price implies a required return of roughly 6-7% on base-case flows or a materially longer up-cycle than the model grants.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
